solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A French king forced to keep English free

parts.note: the French for 'a' is un

indicators.note: the king and the forced pair hold the English letter between them

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
a forced smile is strained

explanation.surface: A French monarch is made to retain an Englishman as a free agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts E between R and STRAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone free of restraint is under no control or limits.

clue.text: Social climber drinks head-free bitter

indicators.note: the drinks lose their head, that is their first letter

parts.note: to sup is to drink, so 'drinks' is sups
a tart taste is sharp or bitter

explanation.surface: A social climber sips a bitter with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-free' drops the S that heads SUPS, leaving UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an upstart is a person who has risen suddenly in status and behaves arrogantly, a social climber.

clue.text: Government's abolishing good checks

indicators.note: the government does away with one letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a monarch's reign is their government; with the 's it becomes reigns

explanation.surface: A government's abolition of good things holds people back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abolishing' takes G out of REIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reins are things that restrain or keep in check, as in keeping a tight rein.

clue.text: Some heartlessly taking cover over attack victim

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed over the next
the outside pair takes another piece in between them
the word some loses its heart, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: a cap is a cover, as on a bottle
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Some cruel people take cover above the victim of an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' is the phrasal verb 'go at', run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is someone blamed and punished for others' faults, a victim.

clue.text: Bank actually deducting a pound

indicators.note: the word for actually has letters taken off it

parts.note: really means in fact, actually
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: The bank actually takes a pound off you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deducting' takes A and L out of REALLY. 'Bank' is the verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bank on something is to depend on it.

clue.text: Business that's fashionable right to use old-fashioned wrapping

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: the old-fashioned word goes round the right letter

parts.note: dusty ideas are old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A trendy firm uses dated packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: industry is commercial activity or a particular trade, business in general.

clue.text: Cheer seeing sweetheart's lie, uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means reading the word bottom to top

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
the heart, the middle letter, of the word sweet

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered on discovering that their lover's lie has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to elate someone is to make them very happy, to cheer them.

clue.text: Abandon clothes after flourish, oddly

indicators.note: the clothes piece comes after the other
take the odd-numbered letters of flourish

parts.note: wear means clothes, as in evening wear

explanation.surface: Someone gives up clothes after a strange flamboyant show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps F, O, R, S from FLOURISH; 'after' puts WEAR behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to forswear is to renounce or give up something, to abandon it.

clue.text: Refuse to overturn plot — knight upset

indicators.note: the plot is turned upside down, read bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the title is reversed

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: Someone declines to overthrow a scheme, and a knight is cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' gives DEB from BED and 'upset' gives RIS from SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is rubbish; debris is scattered waste and rubble.

clue.text: Grew, like some churches, welcoming everybody

indicators.note: the churches take in the other piece

parts.note: many churches are spired, having a spire
all means everybody

explanation.surface: The congregation increased, as at some churches open to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: costs that spiralled grew rapidly and continuously.

clue.text: Stood with person admitted to hospital department

indicators.note: the person is taken into the department, so goes inside it

parts.note: A and E is the accident and emergency department, a British hospital's emergency room
bod is British slang for a person

explanation.surface: A patient waited, admitted to a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood' is the past tense of abide in its sense of tolerate, as in 'could not abide him'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of abide, which means tolerate: one who abode something put up with it.

clue.text: By some means we reach this?

definitions.text: By some means we reach this?

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words are used, the ones lying inside them

explanation.surface: A question about how a puzzle's solution is reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By some' points to letters inside MEANS WE REACH. The whole clue also says what this light is: what solvers reach by some means.
explanation.definitionFit: The solution of a puzzle is what solvers are trying to arrive at by working the clue.

clue.text: Mug shot's first held by ruddy flipping judge!

parts.note: a mug is a fool, an ass

indicators.note: the reversed colour holds the single letter inside it
the colour word is flipped back to front

parts.note: rose is a ruddy, pinkish-red colour

indicators.note: 'first' after shot's asks for only the opening letter of that word

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that a judge is a ruddy flipping fool in a mug shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' gives ESOR from ROSE, and 'held by' puts S inside it. 'ruddy' and 'flipping' pose as mild British curses.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor judges value or performance, or advises a court, so is a kind of judge.

clue.text: Express disapproval about embracing East German

indicators.note: the disapproving sound wraps round the compass letter

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
on means about, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Someone tuts about a German from the East being hugged.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teuton is a member of an ancient Germanic people, by extension a German.

clue.text: Relative touring exotic hot strip

indicators.note: the relative goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: an uncle is a relative

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative visiting a foreign hot spot takes his clothes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to strip is to undress, to remove one's clothes.

clue.text: Continue to find monsters in Paris, occasionally

indicators.note: the monsters go inside the letters from Paris
take every other letter of Paris

parts.note: ogres are monsters

explanation.surface: Carry on to find monsters in Paris now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' keeps P, R, S from PARIS, and 'in' puts OGRES inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to progress is to move forward or carry on.

clue.text: Rude being seen in grand knockout blouse

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the rude word sits inside the knockout's letters

parts.note: a knockout is something excellent, A1, with the digit read as the letter I
ribald means rude or vulgar

explanation.surface: Something rude is spotted in a magnificent, stunning blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A knockout is something first-rate, A1, and the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a loose blouse styled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's followers.

clue.text: Strikers crossing balls finally carrying contest

indicators.note: the crossing carries the contest inside it

parts.note: a ford is a river crossing
a war is a contest

indicators.note: take the last letter of balls

explanation.surface: Footballers take part in a match with balls crossed in at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Football's attackers, the players whose job is to score, are its strikers.

clue.text: Feline pinching old feline's place

indicators.note: the lion grabs and holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
a cat is a feline; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: One big cat stealing an old cat's spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a location is a place or site.

clue.text: Catches girl with very big bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece is placed at the bottom

parts.note: lass is a girl
OS stands for outsize, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A girl with a very large bottom attracts attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' puts OS below LASS. The definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso an animal is to catch it with a looped rope.

clue.text: Alleged region Ark rested, around Turkey initially

definitions.text: Alleged region Ark rested, around Turkey initially

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A description of where Noah's Ark is said to have come to rest, in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letter of every word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey is traditionally where the Ark came to rest after the Flood.

clue.text: Tungsten's estimated to keep most rigid

indicators.note: the words keep the letters held within them

explanation.surface: A metal is estimated to stay at its stiffest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' points to letters inside TUNGSTEN'S ESTIMATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of tense, meaning stretched tight or rigid.

clue.text: News follows Sun's decline

indicators.note: the news comes after the other piece

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
the lowdown is the inside news or information

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sales drop, as The Sun's coverage trails behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts LOWDOWN after S. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, so 'News' and 'Sun' look connected.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a slowdown is a decline in activity or pace.

clue.text: Painter of the French Revolution's first Queen

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

indicators.note: the first letter of revolution

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: An artist depicting the French Revolution's first queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives R from REVOLUTION'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Get over battalion losing regulars

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the battalion loses its even letters, keeping the odd ones

explanation.surface: Recover after a battalion loses its regular soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing regulars' keeps B, T, A, I, N from BATTALION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to obtain something is to acquire it.

clue.text: A wrong righted in operation

indicators.note: the wrong is put right by being turned the other way up

parts.note: an evil is a wrong

explanation.surface: A wrong is corrected during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'righted' turns EVIL into LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A system that is live or working is active and running.

clue.text: Performing captivating exercise topless

indicators.note: the performing word captures the exercise letters inside it

parts.note: an actor who is on is performing
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A performer doing a topless workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like part of the surface picture, but it is the definition: an open car has no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An open car has no roof, so open-topped means topless.

clue.text: Additional worry getting bowled out

indicators.note: the bowled letter is taken out

parts.note: to bother is to worry
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A batsman faces extra worry at being bowled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes B from BOTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: other can mean further or additional, as in other matters.

clue.text: Horrid, almost feverish throb with intravenous injection

indicators.note: the colour word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: a feverish face is flushed red

indicators.note: the abbreviation is injected into the throb, going inside it

parts.note: a pulse is a throb

explanation.surface: A nasty, near-delirious pounding after a drip injection.
explanation.walkthrough: A feverish face is flushed, hence red.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: repulsive means disgusting, horrid.

clue.text: Feeling tender, one's going to specialist medical centre

parts.note: to tender something is to offer or present it
one's read as 'one is', which in the first person is I'm
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Someone feeling tender is off to a specialist clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is I'm, the speaker saying 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is an intuitive feeling that something is about to happen, a foreboding.
